records.source: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֣ר מַלְכָּ֗א עֲבַד֙ לְחֶ֣ם רַ֔ב לְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי אֲלַ֑ף וְלָקֳבֵ֥ל אַלְפָּ֖א חַמְרָ֥א שָׁתֵֽה׃
records.gloss: Belshazzar the king made a feast great for his nobles, a thousand, and before the thousand the wine he was drinking.
pieces: King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in front of them all.

L.1: Belshazzar the king made a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and in front of the thousand he was drinking the wine.

R.1: King Belshazzar gave a big party for a thousand of his important officials. He drank wine with them.

decisions.choice: Belshazzar the king: the son of Nabonidus, who ruled in Babylon in his father's place
decisions.reason: Belshazzar was the eldest son of Nabonidus, the last king of Babylon (556-539 BC). Babylonian records show that Nabonidus spent about ten years away at the oasis of Teima in Arabia and left Belshazzar to rule in Babylon. So Belshazzar acted as king, though the records do not give him that title. This explains why he can offer only the "third" place in the kingdom (verse 7). Between Nebuchadnezzar's death in 562 BC and Nabonidus there were three short reigns, so some twenty-three years lie between chapters 4 and 5.

decisions.choice: before the thousand he was drinking: the king drank in front of his guests
decisions.reason: The king may have sat at a high table facing his guests, or led them in drinking. The detail prepares for verse 2, where the wine leads to his sacrilege.

decisions.choice: a big party (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "party" for "feast", which in the Aramaic is a drinking banquet.

records.heading: Belshazzar's feast

records.source: בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֞ר אֲמַ֣ר׀בִּטְעֵ֣ם חַמְרָ֗א לְהַיְתָיָה֙ לְמָאנֵי֙ דַּהֲבָ֣א וְכַסְפָּ֔א דִּ֤י הַנְפֵּק֙ נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֣ר אֲב֔וּהִי מִן־הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְיִשְׁתּ֣וֹן בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Belshazzar said, in [the] taste of the wine, to bring the vessels of gold and silver which had brought out Nebuchadnezzar his father from the temple which [was] in Jerusalem, that might drink from them the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines.
pieces: While Belshazzar was tasting the wine, he ordered that the gold and silver vessels his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought in, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines could drink from them.

L.2: Belshazzar, under the taste of the wine, said to bring the vessels of gold and of silver that Nebuchadnezzar his father had brought out from the temple that [was] in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines might drink from them.

R.2: After he had been drinking for a while, Belshazzar gave an order. He told his servants to bring the gold and silver cups and bowls that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. He wanted to drink from them with his officials, his wives and his other women.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar his father: his predecessor, or his ancestor
alternatives: his father in the strict sense
decisions.reason: Belshazzar was the son of Nabonidus, not of Nebuchadnezzar. In Aramaic and Hebrew, "father" can mean grandfather, ancestor or predecessor on the throne (compare 2 Kings 14:3), and "son" a descendant or successor. Some think that Nabonidus married a daughter of Nebuchadnezzar, which would make him Belshazzar's grandfather, but this is not certain. The queen (verse 11) and Daniel (verses 18, 22) also call Nebuchadnezzar his father.

decisions.choice: under the taste of the wine: as the wine took hold, or while he tasted it
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean "under the influence of the wine" or "at the tasting of the wine", when the drinking began. Either way, the drinking leads to the order.

decisions.choice: the vessels taken from the temple in Jerusalem: the vessels of 1:2
decisions.reason: These are the temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar carried to Babylon (1:2; 2 Kings 25:13-15). Using holy vessels at a drunken feast, while praising other gods (verse 4), is deliberate contempt for the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: his other women (R)
decisions.reason: Concubines were wives of lower rank. Readable says "his other women".

records.source: בֵּאדַ֗יִן הַיְתִיו֙ מָאנֵ֣י דַהֲבָ֔א דִּ֣י הַנְפִּ֗קוּ מִן־הֵֽיכְלָ֛א דִּֽי־בֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְאִשְׁתִּ֣יו בְּה֗וֹן מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי שֵׁגְלָתֵ֖הּ וּלְחֵנָתֵֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then they brought the vessels of gold which they had brought out from the temple that [was] the house of God which [was] in Jerusalem, and drank from them the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines.
pieces: So the gold vessels that had been carried off from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, were brought in, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.

L.3: Then they brought the vessels of gold that had been taken out of the temple, the house of God, which [was] in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.

R.3: So the gold cups and bowls from God's temple in Jerusalem were brought in. The king, his officials, his wives and his other women drank from them.

decisions.choice: the vessels of gold: the silver of verse 2 is not named
alternatives: the vessels of gold and of silver
decisions.reason: Only the gold vessels are named here; the Greek translation of Theodotion and the Latin add "and of silver", as in verse 2. The difference does not change the sense.

decisions.choice: which they had brought out: which had been taken out
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "which they brought out", with no stated subject, meaning "which had been brought out".

decisions.choice: that had been taken (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the Aramaic "they brought out" as a passive, which is what it means (m2). Literal keeps "the temple, the house of God" as two phrases side by side.

records.source: אִשְׁתִּ֖יו חַמְרָ֑א וְ֠שַׁבַּחוּ לֵֽאלָהֵ֞י דַּהֲבָ֧א וְכַסְפָּ֛א נְחָשָׁ֥א פַרְזְלָ֖א אָעָ֥א וְאַבְנָֽא׃
records.gloss: They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.
pieces: They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, of bronze, iron, wood and stone.

L.4: They drank the wine and praised the gods of gold and of silver, of bronze, of iron, of wood and of stone.

R.4: As they drank, they praised their gods, which were made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.

decisions.choice: gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone: idols
decisions.reason: The list of materials mocks idols as things made by human hands (Deuteronomy 4:28; Psalm 115:4-8; Isaiah 44:9-20). Daniel takes up the same list in verse 23. Gold, silver, bronze and iron are also the metals of the statue of chapter 2.

decisions.choice: their gods, which were made of (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says that the gods were made of these materials.

records.source: בַּהּ־שַׁעֲתָ֗ה נְפַ֨קָה֙ אֶצְבְּעָן֙ דִּ֣י יַד־אֱנָ֔שׁ וְכָֽתְבָן֙ לָקֳבֵ֣ל נֶבְרַשְׁתָּ֔א עַל־גִּירָ֕א דִּֽי־כְתַ֥ל הֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וּמַלְכָּ֣א חָזֵ֔ה פַּ֥ס יְדָ֖ה דִּ֥י כָתְבָֽה׃
records.gloss: At that moment came forth fingers of a hand of a man, and were writing opposite the lampstand on the plaster of [the] wall of the palace of the king; and the king was seeing the palm of the hand that was writing.
pieces: At that very moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and began writing on the plaster of the palace wall, across from the lampstand. The king watched the hand as it wrote.

L.5: At that moment the fingers of a human hand came out and were writing opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace; and the king was watching the palm of the hand that was writing.

R.5: Suddenly, the fingers of a human hand appeared. They began to write on the white wall of the king's palace, next to the lampstand. The king watched the hand as it was writing.

decisions.choice: opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall: where the light fell
decisions.reason: The writing appeared on the white plastered wall, where the lamp lit it so that everyone could see it. Remains of a large hall with plastered walls have been found in the palace at Babylon.

decisions.choice: the palm of the hand: the hand itself, perhaps to the wrist
decisions.reason: The word means the flat of the hand. The king saw only a hand, without a body.

decisions.choice: the white wall (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "white wall" for "the plaster of the wall", since the plaster was white.

records.source: אֱדַ֤יִן מַלְכָּא֙ זִיוֺ֣הִי שְׁנ֔וֹהִי וְרַעיֹנֹ֖הִייְבַהֲלוּנֵּ֑הּ וְקִטְרֵ֤י חַרְצֵהּ֙ מִשְׁתָּרַ֔יִן וְאַ֨רְכֻבָּתֵ֔הּ דָּ֥א לְדָ֖א נָֽקְשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: Then the king, his brightness changed him, and his thoughts alarmed him, and [the] joints of his hips were loosened, and his knees this to this were knocking.
pieces: Then the king turned pale. His thoughts terrified him, his legs gave way, and his knees knocked together.

L.6: Then the king's color changed, and his thoughts alarmed him; and the joints of his hips were loosened, and his knees knocked against each other.

R.6: The king's face turned white. He was so afraid that his legs became weak and his knees shook.

decisions.choice: his brightness changed: the color left his face
decisions.reason: The word means radiance, the glow of a face (4:33). The king turned pale with fear.

decisions.choice: the joints of his hips were loosened: his legs gave way
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures the weakness of terror, when one can no longer stand. Some take it as a loss of control of the bowels, but the text does not say so.

decisions.choice: color (L); turned pale (B); turned white (R); legs gave way (B)
decisions.reason: The idioms are given in plain words (m1, m2). Literal keeps "the joints of his hips".

records.source: קָרֵ֤א מַלְכָּא֙ בְּחַ֔יִל לְהֶֽעָלָה֙ לְאָ֣שְׁפַיָּ֔א כַּשְׂדָּאֵ֖י וְגָזְרַיָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר׀לְחַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֗ל דִּ֣י כָל־אֱ֠נָשׁ דִּֽי־יִקְרֵ֞ה כְּתָבָ֣ה דְנָ֗ה וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ יְחַוִּנַּ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א יִלְבַּ֗שׁ וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֤אדִֽי־דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֔הּ וְתַלְתִּ֥י בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א יִשְׁלַֽט׃ס
records.gloss: Calling the king with strength to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners; answering the king and saying to the wise men of Babylon: any man who reads this writing and its interpretation declares to me, purple he will be clothed, and the chain of gold [will be] on his neck, and third in the kingdom he will rule.
pieces: The king shouted for the enchanters, Chaldeans and diviners to be brought in. The king said to the wise men of Babylon, "Anyone who can read this writing and tell me what it means will be dressed in purple and have a gold chain around his neck, and he will be the third ruler in the kingdom."

L.7: The king called out with strength to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners. The king answered and said to the wise men of Babylon, "Any person who reads this writing and declares to me its interpretation will be clothed with purple and [have] the chain of gold on his neck, and will rule as third in the kingdom."

R.7: The king shouted for his enchanters, astrologers and diviners to come. He said to these wise men of Babylon, "I will reward anyone who can read this writing and tell me what it means. I will dress him in purple robes like a king, and put a gold chain around his neck. He will be the third most powerful ruler in my kingdom."

decisions.choice: purple and a gold chain: marks of royal honor
decisions.reason: Purple cloth was costly and was worn by kings and their highest officials (Esther 8:15). A gold chain around the neck was a sign of high office, as with Joseph (Genesis 41:42).

decisions.choice: third in the kingdom: third in rank, after Nabonidus and Belshazzar
alternatives: one of three officers who governed the kingdom
decisions.reason: The word means "third" or perhaps the title of a high officer, "one of three". If Nabonidus was king and Belshazzar ruled for him (verse 1), the third place was the highest Belshazzar could give.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: a class of experts
decisions.reason: As in 2:2 and 4:4. The list is shorter here, but it is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: enchanters, Chaldeans, diviners (L, B); enchanters, astrologers, diviners (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms for Daniel set, the list is kept at every level, with "astrologers" at Readable for the Chaldeans as a class of experts. Readable makes plain that purple was worn by kings.

records.source: אֱדַ֨יִן֙ עָֽלִּ֔ין כֹּ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֣י מַלְכָּ֑א וְלָֽא־כָהֲלִ֤ין כְּתָבָא֙ לְמִקְרֵ֔א וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לְהוֹדָעָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃
records.gloss: Then came in all [the] wise men of the king, and not were they able the writing to read, and its interpretation to make known to the king.
pieces: Then all the king's wise men came in, but none of them could read the writing or tell the king what it meant.

L.8: Then all the wise men of the king came in, but they were not able to read the writing or to make known its interpretation to the king.

R.8: All the king's wise men came in. But none of them could read the writing or tell the king what it meant.

decisions.choice: they could not read the writing: not even the words
decisions.reason: The wise men could not even read the words, let alone explain them. Why is not said: the script may have been unknown to them, or the words written without vowels and so open to several readings (see verse 25), or God hid the meaning from them.

decisions.choice: the order of the Aramaic kept in the gloss
decisions.reason: The Aramaic puts "the writing" before "to read"; all three levels use normal English order.

records.heading: The wise men fail

records.source: אֱ֠דַיִן מַלְכָּ֤א בֵלְשַׁאצַּר֙ שַׂגִּ֣יא מִתְבָּהַ֔ל וְזִיוֺ֖הִי שָׁנַ֣יִן עֲל֑וֹהִי וְרַבְרְבָנ֖וֹהִי מִֽשְׁתַּבְּשִֽׁין׃
records.gloss: Then the king Belshazzar [was] greatly alarmed, and his brightness [was] changing upon him, and his nobles [were] perplexed.
pieces: Then King Belshazzar became even more terrified and his face grew pale, and his nobles were bewildered.

L.9: Then King Belshazzar was greatly alarmed, and his color changed upon him, and his nobles were perplexed.

R.9: So King Belshazzar became even more afraid, and his face turned white. His officials did not know what to do.

decisions.choice: his color changed: as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The king's fear grows when his experts fail.

decisions.choice: even more (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "even more", since the king was already afraid (verse 6).

records.source: מַלְכְּתָ֕א לָקֳבֵ֨ל מִלֵּ֤י מַלְכָּא֙ וְרַבְרְבָנ֔וֹהִי לְבֵ֥ית מִשְׁתְּיָ֖א עַלַּ֑ת עֲנָ֨ת מַלְכְּתָ֜א וַאֲמֶ֗רֶת מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י אַֽל־יְבַהֲלוּךְ֙ רַעְיוֹנָ֔ךְ וְזִיוָ֖יךְ אַל־יִשְׁתַּנּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: The queen, because of [the] words of the king and his nobles, into the house of the feast came in; answering the queen and saying: O king, forever live! Let not your thoughts alarm you, and your brightness let not be changed.
pieces: The queen, hearing the voices of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet hall. The queen said, "O king, may you live forever! Do not be alarmed, and do not let your face grow pale.

L.10: The queen, because of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet hall. The queen answered and said, "O king, live forever! Let not your thoughts alarm you, and let not your color be changed.

R.10: The queen mother heard the king and his officials talking, and she came into the banquet hall. She said, "Your Majesty, may you live forever! Do not be afraid. Do not look so pale.

decisions.choice: the queen: probably the queen mother
decisions.reason: Belshazzar's wives are already at the feast (verse 2). This queen knows the history of Nebuchadnezzar's reign and speaks with authority, so she is most likely the king's mother or grandmother, who held high rank at court (compare 1 Kings 15:13; Jeremiah 13:18). Some identify her with a wife of Nebuchadnezzar or with the mother of Nabonidus, but the text does not name her.

decisions.choice: O king, live forever: the greeting of the court
decisions.reason: As in 2:4 and 3:9.

decisions.choice: The queen mother (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names her as "the queen mother", the most likely sense (m1), so that young readers do not take her for Belshazzar's wife. Literal and Balanced keep "the queen".

records.source: אִיתַ֨י גְּבַ֜ר בְּמַלְכוּתָ֗ךְ דִּ֠י ר֣וּחַ אֱלָהִ֣ין קַדִּישִׁין֮ בֵּהּ֒ וּבְיוֹמֵ֣י אֲב֗וּךְ נַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה כְּחָכְמַת־אֱלָהִ֖ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֣חַת בֵּ֑הּ וּמַלְכָּ֤א נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּר֙ אֲב֔וּךְ רַ֧ב חַרְטֻמִּ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין כַּשְׂדָּאִין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין הֲקִימֵ֖הּ אֲב֥וּךְ מַלְכָּֽא׃
records.gloss: There is a man in your kingdom in whom [is] a spirit of gods holy, and in [the] days of your father illumination and insight and wisdom like [the] wisdom of gods was found in him; and the king Nebuchadnezzar your father, chief of magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, diviners, appointed him, your father the king,
pieces: In your kingdom there is a man in whom the spirit of the holy gods lives. In your father's time he showed insight, understanding and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans and diviners. Yes, your father the king did this,

L.11: There is a man in your kingdom in whom [is] a spirit of [the] holy gods. And in your father's days illumination and insight and wisdom like [the] wisdom of gods were found in him; and King Nebuchadnezzar your father made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans [and] diviners; your father the king [did],

R.11: In your kingdom there is a man who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. When your father was king, this man showed that he had understanding and great wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar, put him in charge of all the magicians, enchanters, astrologers and diviners.

decisions.choice: a spirit of the holy gods ... the wisdom of the gods: a polytheist's words
decisions.reason: The queen uses Nebuchadnezzar's words of 4:5-6, 15, and speaks as a worshiper of many gods. See the note at 4:5.

decisions.choice: light and insight and wisdom: understanding that sees into hidden things
decisions.reason: "Light" here means enlightenment, the gift of seeing what is hidden (2:22).

decisions.choice: chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, diviners: as in 2:48 and 4:6
decisions.reason: The list of experts of 4:4 is kept. "Chaldeans" here is the class of experts.

decisions.choice: the list kept; the repeated "your father the king" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The list of experts is kept at every level, with "astrologers" at Readable. The queen repeats "your father the king" for emphasis; Literal and Balanced keep the repetition, and Readable leaves it out.

records.source: כָּל־קֳבֵ֡ל דִּ֣י ר֣וּחַ׀יַתִּירָ֡ה וּמַנְדַּ֡ע וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֡וּ מְפַשַּׁ֣ר חֶלְמִין֩ וַֽאַֽחֲוָיַ֨ת אֲחִידָ֜ן וּמְשָׁרֵ֣א קִטְרִ֗ין הִשְׁתְּכַ֤חַת בֵּהּ֙ בְּדָ֣נִיֵּ֔אל דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֥א שָׂם־שְׁמֵ֖הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר כְּעַ֛ן דָּנִיֵּ֥אל יִתְקְרֵ֖י וּפִשְׁרָ֥ה יְהַֽחֲוֵֽה׃פ
records.gloss: because that a spirit extraordinary and knowledge and insight, interpreting of dreams and declaring of riddles and loosening of knots, was found in him, in Daniel, whom the king made his name Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and the interpretation he will declare.
pieces: because this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, knowledge and understanding to interpret dreams, explain riddles and solve hard problems. So now let Daniel be called, and he will tell you what the writing means."

L.12: because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge and insight, interpreting dreams, explaining riddles and loosening knots, were found in him, in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be summoned, and the interpretation he will declare."

R.12: This man, Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, has an excellent mind. He has knowledge and understanding. He can explain the meaning of dreams and riddles, and he can solve hard problems. So send for Daniel. He will tell you what the writing means."

decisions.choice: loosening knots: solving hard problems
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean solving difficult problems, or undoing magic knots and spells, a task of Babylon's experts. The same words return in verse 16.

decisions.choice: an extraordinary spirit: an exceptional mind
decisions.reason: The phrase means an outstanding spirit or ability (6:4).

decisions.choice: solve hard problems (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "loosening knots"; Balanced and Readable give the more likely sense (m1).

records.source: בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל הֻעַ֖ל קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֗אל אַנְתְּ־ה֤וּא דָנִיֵּאל֙ דִּֽי־מִן־בְּנֵ֤י גָלוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְה֔וּד דִּ֥י הַיְתִ֛י מַלְכָּ֥א אַ֖בִי מִן־יְהֽוּד׃
records.gloss: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. Answering the king and saying to Daniel: You are that Daniel who [is] from the sons of the exile of Judah, whom brought the king my father from Judah?
pieces: So Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king said to him, "Are you that Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, whom my father the king brought from Judah?

L.13: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king answered and said to Daniel, "Are you that Daniel who is one of the exiles of Judah, whom the king my father brought from Judah?

R.13: So Daniel was brought to the king. The king said to him, "So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father the king brought here from Judah.

decisions.choice: you are that Daniel: a question or a statement
decisions.reason: The Aramaic can be a question ("Are you that Daniel ...?") or a statement ("You are that Daniel ..."). Either way, the king speaks of Daniel with some disdain, as a captive.

decisions.choice: the exiles of Judah: as in 2:25
decisions.reason: Daniel had been taken from Judah some sixty-six years before (1:1). The king knows of him, but only as a foreign captive.

decisions.choice: So you are Daniel (R)
decisions.reason: Readable takes the statement reading, which Literal and Balanced's question also allows (m1).

records.heading: Daniel before Belshazzar

records.source: וְשִׁמְעֵ֣ת עֲלָ֔ךְ דִּ֛י ר֥וּחַ אֱלָהִ֖ין בָּ֑ךְ וְנַהִיר֧וּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנ֛וּ וְחָכְמָ֥ה יַתִּירָ֖ה הִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַת בָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And I have heard concerning you that a spirit of gods [is] in you, and illumination and insight and wisdom extraordinary is found in you.
pieces: I have heard about you: the spirit of the gods is in you, and you have insight, understanding and extraordinary wisdom.

L.14: I have heard of you, that a spirit of [the] gods [is] in you, and that light and insight and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.

R.14: I have been told that the spirit of the gods is in you. I have heard that you have understanding and great wisdom.

decisions.choice: a spirit of gods: the king leaves out "holy"
decisions.reason: Unlike Nebuchadnezzar and the queen (4:5; 5:11), Belshazzar says only "a spirit of gods". Some see in this his lack of reverence, but the text does not comment.

decisions.choice: light (L); insight (B); understanding (R)
decisions.reason: The three words for understanding are kept at Literal and Balanced; Readable joins them.

records.source: וּכְעַ֞ן הֻעַ֣לּוּ קָֽדָמַ֗י חַכִּֽימַיָּא֙ אָֽשְׁפַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־כְתָבָ֤ה דְנָה֙ יִקְר֔וֹן וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ לְהוֹדָעֻתַ֑נִי וְלָֽא־כָהֲלִ֥ין פְּשַֽׁר־מִלְּתָ֖א לְהַחֲוָיָֽה׃
records.gloss: And now have been brought in before me the wise men, the enchanters, that this writing they might read and its interpretation make known to me, and not were they able the interpretation of the matter to declare.
pieces: The wise men and enchanters were brought in before me to read this writing and tell me what it means, but they could not explain it.

L.15: And now there have been brought in before me the wise men, the enchanters, so that this writing they might read and its interpretation make known to me; but they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.

R.15: My wise men and enchanters were brought to me to read this writing and tell me what it means. But they could not explain it.

decisions.choice: the wise men, the enchanters: the experts in general
decisions.reason: The two words stand side by side without "and": the wise men, that is, the enchanters. The king means all his experts.

decisions.choice: and enchanters (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two with "and".

records.source: וַאֲנָה֙ שִׁמְעֵ֣ת עֲלָ֔ךְ דִּֽי־תִיכּ֥וּלפִּשְׁרִ֛ין לְמִפְשַׁ֖ר וְקִטְרִ֣ין לְמִשְׁרֵ֑א כְּעַ֡ן הֵן֩ תִּכ֨וּל כְּתָבָ֜א לְמִקְרֵ֗א וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ לְהוֹדָ֣עֻתַ֔נִי אַרְגְּוָנָ֣א תִלְבַּ֗שׁ וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֤אדִֽי־דַהֲבָא֙ עַֽל־צַוְּארָ֔ךְ וְתַלְתָּ֥א בְמַלְכוּתָ֖א תִּשְׁלַֽט׃פ
records.gloss: And I have heard concerning you that you are able interpretations to interpret and knots to loosen. Now, if you are able the writing to read and its interpretation to make known to me, purple you will be clothed, and the chain of gold [will be] on your neck, and third in the kingdom you will rule.
pieces: But I have heard that you can give interpretations and solve hard problems. Now if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will be dressed in purple and have a gold chain around your neck, and you will be the third ruler in the kingdom."

L.16: But I have heard of you, that you are able to give interpretations and to loosen knots. Now if you are able to read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you will be clothed with purple, and [have] the chain of gold on your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom."

R.16: But I have heard that you can explain things and solve hard problems. If you can read this writing and tell me what it means, I will dress you in purple robes like a king and put a gold chain around your neck. You will be the third most powerful ruler in my kingdom."

decisions.choice: purple, the gold chain, third in the kingdom: the offer of verse 7
decisions.reason: The king repeats his offer to Daniel.

decisions.choice: solve hard problems (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֜יִן עָנֵ֣ה דָנִיֵּ֗אל וְאָמַר֙ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א מַתְּנָתָךְ֙ לָ֣ךְ לֶֽהֶוְיָ֔ן וּנְבָ֥זְבְּיָתָ֖ךְ לְאָחֳרָ֣ן הַ֑ב בְּרַ֗ם כְּתָבָא֙ אֶקְרֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֔א וּפִשְׁרָ֖א אֲהוֹדְעִנֵּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Then answering Daniel and saying before the king: Your gifts let them be for yourself, and your rewards to another give; however, the writing I will read to the king, and the interpretation I will make known to him.
pieces: Then Daniel answered the king, "You may keep your gifts and give your rewards to someone else. Still, I will read the writing for the king and tell him what it means.

L.17: Then Daniel answered and said before the king, "Your gifts, let them be for yourself, and your rewards give to another; however, the writing I will read to the king, and the interpretation I will make known to him.

R.17: Daniel answered the king, "You can keep your gifts, or give them to someone else. But I will read the writing for you, Your Majesty, and tell you what it means.

decisions.choice: keep your gifts: Daniel will not be bought
decisions.reason: Daniel refuses the reward, not out of rudeness but so that no one could think that he spoke to please the king. He is about to deliver a sentence of judgment. In verse 29, after he has spoken, the king honors him anyway.

decisions.choice: for you, Your Majesty (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the courtly third person "to the king" into direct address.

records.heading: Daniel reads the writing

records.source: אַ֖נְתְּ מַלְכָּ֑א אֱלָהָא֙ עִלָּאָ֔ה מַלְכוּתָ֤א וּרְבוּתָא֙ וִיקָרָ֣א וְהַדְרָ֔ה יְהַ֖ב לִנְבֻכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר אֲבֽוּךְ׃
records.gloss: You, O king, God Most High the kingdom and the greatness and the glory and the majesty gave to Nebuchadnezzar your father.
pieces: O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar the kingdom, greatness, glory and majesty.

L.18: You, O king: the Most High God gave the kingdom and the greatness and the glory and the majesty to Nebuchadnezzar your father.

R.18: Your Majesty, the Most High God made your father Nebuchadnezzar a great and powerful king. God gave him honor and glory.

decisions.choice: the kingdom, greatness, glory and majesty: as in 2:37 and 4:27, 33
decisions.reason: Daniel begins by reminding Belshazzar of the lesson of chapter 4: Nebuchadnezzar's power came from God (2:37). The words "glory" and "majesty" were the very things Nebuchadnezzar boasted of (4:27) and received back (4:33).

decisions.choice: the Most High God at every level
decisions.reason: The terms for Daniel set "the Most High" at every level.

records.source: וּמִן־רְבוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְהַב־לֵ֔הּ כֹּ֣ל עַֽמְמַיָּ֗א אֻמַיָּא֙ וְלִשָּׁ֣נַיָּ֔א הֲו֛וֹ זָיְעִ֥ין וְדָחֲלִ֖ין מִן־קֳדָמ֑וֹהִי דִּֽי־הֲוָ֨ה צָבֵ֜א הֲוָ֣א קָטֵ֗ל וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מַחֵ֔א וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֤ה צָבֵא֙ הֲוָ֣ה מָרִ֔ים וְדִֽי־הֲוָ֥ה צָבֵ֖א הֲוָ֥ה מַשְׁפִּֽיל׃
records.gloss: And because of the greatness that he gave him, all the peoples, nations and languages were trembling and fearing before him; whom he wished he was killing, and whom he wished he was keeping alive, and whom he wished he was raising, and whom he wished he was humbling.
pieces: Because of the greatness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him, all the peoples, nations and people of every language trembled and were afraid of him. He put to death anyone he wanted to, and let live anyone he wanted to. He raised up anyone he wanted to, and humbled anyone he wanted to.

L.19: And from the greatness {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to him, all the peoples, nations and languages were trembling and fearing before him. Whom he wished he killed, and whom he wished he kept alive; whom he wished he raised up, and whom he wished he humbled.

R.19: God made him so great that people of every nation and language trembled with fear in front of him. If he wanted to kill someone, he did. If he wanted to let someone live, he did. If he wanted to make someone important, he did. If he wanted to bring someone down, he did.

decisions.choice: whom he wished he killed ...: absolute human power
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar held the power of life and death over his subjects. The four pairs of words describe what God alone truly holds (1 Samuel 2:6-7). The danger of such power is that a king forgets that it was given him (verse 20).

decisions.choice: that he gave him: God gave Nebuchadnezzar
decisions.reason: The "he" who gave is the Most High God of verse 18; the "him" who received is Nebuchadnezzar. From there on, "he" is Nebuchadnezzar.

decisions.choice: a divine pronoun only for God
decisions.reason: Only the first "he", which is God (m2), takes the divine pronoun setting. Readable names God and repeats "he did" to keep the rhythm of the four pairs.

records.source: וּכְדִי֙ רִ֣ם לִבְבֵ֔הּ וְרוּחֵ֖הּ תִּֽקְפַ֣ת לַהֲזָדָ֑ה הָנְחַת֙ מִן־כָּרְסֵ֣א מַלְכוּתֵ֔הּ וִֽיקָרָ֖ה הֶעְדִּ֥יוּ מִנֵּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And when was lifted up his heart and his spirit grew hard to act proudly, he was brought down from [the] throne of his kingdom, and the glory they took from him.
pieces: But when his heart became proud and his spirit hardened in arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne and his glory was stripped from him.

L.20: But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit grew hard so that he acted proudly, he was brought down from the throne of his kingdom, and his glory was taken from him.

R.20: But he became proud and stubborn and arrogant. So he was removed from his throne, and his honor was taken away from him.

decisions.choice: his heart was lifted up, his spirit grew hard: pride and stubbornness
decisions.reason: A "lifted up" heart is pride (Deuteronomy 8:14; Ezekiel 28:2). "Grew hard" or "grew strong" is the stubbornness of one who will not listen, like Pharaoh's hardened heart (Exodus 7:13).

decisions.choice: they took his glory: his glory was taken
decisions.reason: The Aramaic "they took" has no named subject; it means "was taken", by God's decree (4:28).

decisions.choice: his glory was taken (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives the Aramaic "they took" as a passive (m2).

records.source: וּמִן־בְּנֵי֩ אֲנָשָׁ֨א טְרִ֜יד וְלִבְבֵ֣הּ׀עִם־חֵיוְתָ֣א שַׁוִּ֗יְווְעִם־עֲרָֽדַיָּא֙ מְדוֹרֵ֔הּ עִשְׂבָּ֤א כְתוֹרִין֙ יְטַ֣עֲמוּנֵּ֔הּ וּמִטַּ֥ל שְׁמַיָּ֖א גִּשְׁמֵ֣הּ יִצְטַבַּ֑ע עַ֣ד דִּֽי־יְדַ֗ע דִּֽי־שַׁלִּ֞יט אֱלָהָ֤א עִלָּאָה֙ בְּמַלְכ֣וּת אֲנָשָׁ֔א וּלְמַן־דִּ֥י יִצְבֵּ֖ה יְהָקֵ֥ים עֲלַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And from [the] sons of humankind he was driven, and his heart with the beasts was made like, and with the wild donkeys [was] his dwelling; grass like oxen they fed him, and from [the] dew of the heavens his body was wet, until that he knew that rules God Most High over [the] kingdom of humankind, and whomever he wills he sets up over it.
pieces: He was driven away from people, and his mind was made like that of an animal. He lived with the wild donkeys and was fed grass like cattle, and his body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until he came to know that the Most High God rules over human kingdoms and sets over them anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chooses.

L.21: And he was driven from the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}, and his heart was made like [that of] the animals, and with the wild donkeys [was] his dwelling; grass like oxen they fed him, and from the dew of the heavens his body was wet, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humankind and sets over it whomever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wills.

R.21: He was forced to leave people, and his mind became like an animal's mind. He lived with the wild donkeys and ate grass like a cow. He was wet with dew every morning. This went on until he understood that the Most High God rules over all the kingdoms of the world. God puts anyone {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants to in charge of them.

decisions.choice: the story of chapter 4
decisions.reason: Daniel retells Nebuchadnezzar's humbling (4:22, 29-30), adding that he lived with the wild donkeys, animals of the open desert (Job 39:5-8).

decisions.choice: the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humankind: the lesson of chapter 4
decisions.reason: The refrain of 4:14, 22 and 29 is repeated as the lesson Belshazzar should have learned.

decisions.choice: the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} (L); people (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:38. Each level follows its wording of 4:22 and 4:29 closely where the words are the same. Literal keeps the Aramaic "they fed him", which means "he was fed" (compare 4:22).

records.source: וְאַ֤נְתְּ בְּרֵהּ֙ בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֔ר לָ֥א הַשְׁפֵּ֖לְתְּ לִבְבָ֑ךְ כָּל־קֳבֵ֕ל דִּ֥י כָל־דְּנָ֖ה יְדַֽעְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And you, his son, Belshazzar, not have you humbled your heart, because that all this you knew.
pieces: But you, Belshazzar, his son, have not humbled yourself, even though you knew all this.

L.22: And you, his son, Belshazzar, you have not brought low your heart, although all this you knew.

R.22: But you, Belshazzar, who are his son, have not been humble, even though you knew all this.

decisions.choice: you have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this
decisions.reason: Belshazzar's guilt is greater because he knew what had happened to Nebuchadnezzar and did not learn from it.

decisions.choice: his son: his descendant or successor
decisions.reason: On "son" and "father" here, see verse 2.

decisions.choice: though you knew (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "because you knew all this"; the sense is "although", which each level gives.

records.source: וְעַ֣ל מָרֵֽא־שְׁמַיָּ֣א׀הִתְרוֹמַ֡מְתָּ וּלְמָֽאנַיָּ֨א דִֽי־בַיְתֵ֜הּ הַיְתִ֣יו קָֽדָמָ֗ךְ וְאַ֨נְתְּ וְרַבְרְבָנָ֜ךְשֵֽׁגְלָתָ֣ךְ וּלְחֵנָתָךְ֮ חַמְרָא֮ שָׁתַ֣יִן בְּהוֹן֒ וְלֵֽאלָהֵ֣י כַסְפָּֽא־וְ֠דַהֲבָא נְחָשָׁ֨א פַרְזְלָ֜א אָעָ֣א וְאַבְנָ֗א דִּ֠י לָֽא־חָזַ֧יִן וְלָא־שָׁמְעִ֛ין וְלָ֥א יָדְעִ֖ין שַׁבַּ֑חְתָּ וְלֵֽאלָהָ֞א דִּֽי־נִשְׁמְתָ֥ךְ בִּידֵ֛הּ וְכָל־אֹרְחָתָ֥ךְ לֵ֖הּ לָ֥א הַדַּֽרְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And against [the] Lord of the heavens you have lifted yourself up, and the vessels of his house they have brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines, wine [are] drinking from them; and the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see and do not hear and do not know, you have praised; and the God in whose hand [is] your breath and all your ways [are] his, him you have not glorified.
pieces: Instead, you have set yourself up against the Lord of heaven. You had the vessels from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house brought to you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood and stone, which neither see nor hear nor understand. Yet you have not honored the God who holds your life in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and controls everything you do.

L.23: But you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven, and the vessels of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} house have been brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines, have been drinking wine from them. And you have praised the gods of silver and gold, of bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know; but the God in whose hand [is] your breath, and whose [are] all your ways, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} you have not glorified.

R.23: You have acted proudly against the Lord of heaven. You had the cups and bowls from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple brought to you. Then you and your officials, your wives and your other women drank wine from them. You praised gods made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone. These gods cannot see or hear or understand anything. But you have not honored the God who gives you every breath you take. He controls everything you do.

decisions.choice: gods that do not see or hear or know: idols
decisions.reason: The words echo the mockery of idols in Deuteronomy 4:28 and Psalm 115:4-7, which have eyes but do not see and ears but do not hear.

decisions.choice: in whose hand is your breath, and whose are all your ways: God holds your life and all you do
decisions.reason: Breath is life itself (Genesis 2:7; Job 12:10). "Your ways" are the course of a person's life. The God the king insulted was the one on whom his every breath depended.

decisions.choice: the Lord of heaven: God as ruler over all
decisions.reason: The title is close to "the God of heaven" (2:18) and "the King of heaven" (4:34).

decisions.choice: divine pronouns for God
decisions.reason: "His house" and "him" refer to God and take the divine pronoun setting. Readable splits the long verse into short sentences.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֨יִן֙ מִן־קֳדָמ֔וֹהִי שְׁלִ֖יַחַפַּסָּ֣א דִֽי־יְדָ֑א וּכְתָבָ֥א דְנָ֖ה רְשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: Then from before him was sent the palm of the hand, and this writing was inscribed.
pieces: That is why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent the hand that wrote this inscription.

L.24: Then from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} presence the palm of the hand was sent, and this writing was inscribed.

R.24: That is why God sent the hand to write these words.

decisions.choice: from his presence the hand was sent: the writing came from God
decisions.reason: Daniel makes plain that the hand that wrote came from the God the king insulted (verse 23).

decisions.choice: That is why he sent (B); That is why God sent (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive into the active and make God the subject.

records.source: וּדְנָ֥ה כְתָבָ֖א דִּ֣י רְשִׁ֑ים מְנֵ֥א מְנֵ֖א תְּקֵ֥ל וּפַרְסִֽין׃
records.gloss: And this [is] the writing which was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN.
pieces: This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN.

L.25: And this [is] the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN.

R.25: These are the words that were written: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN.

decisions.choice: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN: the names of weights, read as verbs
decisions.reason: The words are Aramaic names of weights or coins: the mina (MENE), the shekel (TEKEL, worth a sixtieth of a mina) and half-minas (PARSIN, "halves"; the singular is PERES, verse 28). Read only as nouns, the words make no sense, which may be why the wise men could not explain them. Daniel reads each one as a verb from the same root: MENE as "numbered", TEKEL as "weighed", and PERES as "divided" (verses 26-28). PERES also sounds like *paras*, "Persia": the kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians. Why MENE is written twice is not certain; it may be for emphasis, or the first may be a verb, "counted".

decisions.choice: and PARSIN: the plural of PERES, with "and"
decisions.reason: PARSIN is the plural of PERES (verse 28), with the Aramaic word for "and" joined to it. In verse 28 Daniel uses the singular.

decisions.choice: MENE, MENE, TEKEL and PARSIN in capitals at every level
decisions.reason: As the terms for Daniel set, the Aramaic words are written in Latin letters and capitals at every level, as an inscription. They are not translated here; Daniel explains them in verses 26-28.

records.source: דְּנָ֖ה פְּשַֽׁר־מִלְּתָ֑א מְנֵ֕א מְנָֽה־אֱלָהָ֥א מַלְכוּתָ֖ךְ וְהַשְׁלְמַֽהּ׃
records.gloss: This [is] the interpretation of the matter: MENE, God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
pieces: This is what the words mean: MENE: God has numbered the days of your kingdom and brought it to an end.

L.26: This [is] the interpretation of the matter: MENE, God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end;

R.26: This is what the words mean: MENE means that God has counted the days of your kingdom, and it is ending.

decisions.choice: MENE, God has numbered your kingdom: its days are counted and finished
decisions.reason: MENE sounds like the verb "to number, count". God has counted out the days of the kingdom, and they are at an end (compare Psalm 90:12).

decisions.choice: the days of (B, R); means that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "the days of" to show what is counted. Readable says "MENE means", as the terms for Daniel allow, since Daniel himself gives the meaning.

records.source: תְּקֵ֑ל תְּקִ֥ילְתָּה בְמֹֽאזַנְיָ֖א וְהִשְׁתְּכַ֥חַתְּ חַסִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: TEKEL, you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking.
pieces: TEKEL: you have been weighed on the scales and found too light.

L.27: TEKEL, you have been weighed in the scales and found lacking;

R.27: TEKEL means that you have been weighed on a scale and found not good enough.

decisions.choice: TEKEL, you have been weighed and found lacking
decisions.reason: TEKEL sounds like the verb "to weigh". The king has been weighed like silver on a scale, and he is too light: he does not have the worth he should (compare Job 31:6; Psalm 62:10).

decisions.choice: not good enough (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what being found too light means.

records.source: פְּרֵ֑ס פְּרִיסַת֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ךְ וִיהִיבַ֖ת לְמָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃
records.gloss: PERES, has been divided your kingdom and given to [the] Medes and Persians.
pieces: PERES: your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."

L.28: PERES, your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians."

R.28: PERES means that your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and the Persians."

decisions.choice: PERES, divided, and given to the Persians: a double pun
decisions.reason: PERES, the singular of PARSIN (verse 25), sounds like the verb "to divide" and like the word for "Persia". The kingdom is broken up and handed over to the Medes and Persians.

decisions.choice: the Medes and Persians: the empire that took Babylon
decisions.reason: Cyrus, king of Persia, had united the Medes and Persians under his rule; his army took Babylon in 539 BC. Daniel speaks of the two peoples together, as in 6:9, 13, 16 and 8:20.

decisions.choice: PERES in capitals at every level
decisions.reason: As in verse 25. Daniel's words end here.

records.source: בֵּאדַ֣יִן׀אֲמַ֣ר בֵּלְשַׁאצַּ֗ר וְהַלְבִּ֤ישׁוּ לְדָֽנִיֵּאל֙ אַרְגְּוָנָ֔א וְהַֽמְנִיכָ֥א דִֽי־דַהֲבָ֖א עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֑הּ וְהַכְרִ֣זֽוּ עֲל֔וֹהִי דִּֽי־לֶהֱוֵ֥א שַׁלִּ֛יט תַּלְתָּ֖א בְּמַלְכוּתָֽא׃
records.gloss: Then said Belshazzar, and they clothed Daniel [with] the purple, and the chain of gold on his neck, and proclaimed concerning him that he would be ruler third in the kingdom.
pieces: Then at Belshazzar's command Daniel was dressed in purple, a gold chain was put around his neck, and it was proclaimed that he would be the third ruler in the kingdom.

L.29: Then Belshazzar gave orders, and they clothed Daniel with purple, [put] the chain of gold on his neck, and made a proclamation concerning him that he would be the third ruler in the kingdom.

R.29: Then Belshazzar gave an order. His servants dressed Daniel in purple robes and put a gold chain around his neck. And the king announced that Daniel was the third most powerful ruler in the kingdom.

decisions.choice: the king keeps his word: Daniel is honored, though he refused
decisions.reason: Belshazzar gives Daniel the promised reward (verse 16), though Daniel had refused it (verse 17) and the kingdom it was part of was about to end.

decisions.choice: His servants (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who did the dressing.

records.source: בֵּ֚הּ בְּלֵ֣ילְיָ֔א קְטִ֕יל בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּ֥א כַשְׂדָּאָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: On that night was killed Belshazzar the king, the Chaldean.
pieces: That very night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.

L.30: That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.

R.30: That same night Belshazzar, the Babylonian king, was killed.

decisions.choice: that very night: the fall of Babylon in 539 BC
decisions.reason: Babylon fell to the army of Cyrus in October 539 BC. Babylonian records say that the city was taken without a battle; the Greek historians Herodotus and Xenophon tell that it fell while the people were feasting, and Xenophon that the king was killed. Daniel tells only that Belshazzar was killed that night.

decisions.choice: the Chaldean: the people who ruled Babylon
decisions.reason: Here "Chaldean" is the people, not the class of experts: Belshazzar was the king of the Chaldean dynasty.

decisions.choice: Chaldean (L, B); Babylonian (R)
decisions.reason: Where the word means the people, the terms for Daniel set "Babylonians" at Readable.
